title: Findings with no game location can never corroborate
body:
Findings that are not about a game location can never corroborate, because clustering is
keyed on location and `locationKey` gives every `unmapped` report its own key (built from
its raw wording). Two reports of one defect written in two wordings are, structurally, two
different places.

Observed live. Two QA leads independently reported the SAME harness defect — the
`inspect_overworld_session_story` MCP tool advertises an empty parameter schema
(`{"properties":{},"type":"object"}`) while rejecting calls that omit `story_choice_id`.
They wrote its location as:

    "MCP tool inspect_overworld_session_story"
    "MCP tool schema for inspect_overworld_session_story"

Both canonicalize to `unmapped`, keyed on those two distinct strings, so they produced two
tickets at report_count 1 — and they even disagreed on severity (S2 vs S3). Independent
agreement by two reporters, the single strongest signal triage exists to detect, was
discarded by construction.

This is now the dominant remaining cause of cluster fragmentation. The embedded-id fix in
`canonicalizeLocation` (rung 1b) resolved the in-game half: reports citing a room id in
prose now share a location and merge. Harness, tooling, and cross-cutting findings have no
game location to cite, so they stay one-per-report.

The current behavior is deliberate and the comment on `locationKey` argues for it: two
unresolved raw strings must not be assumed to be the same place. That is right for prose
that FAILED to resolve. It is wrong for reports that are not about a place at all — there
is no third state today, so both collapse into the same conservative refusal.

Worth considering (design call, not a prescription):
  - A `surface` location kind for non-game targets (tool name, CLI, docs), canonicalized
    from a known list of tool names the way game ids are, so two wordings of one tool name
    share a key.
  - Or: let pass 2 merge across `unmapped` keys on token similarity alone, at a higher
    Jaccard threshold than the in-location one, accepting that a false merge of two
    unresolved prose reports is cheaper than never corroborating any of them.

Evidence: 6 sessions, 55 issues. Before the rung-1b fix: 55 clusters, every one
report_count 1. After: 53 clusters with one genuine cluster of 3. The ceiling on further
merging is now almost entirely unmapped reports.

evidence.summary: Two leads reported one harness defect; it became two tickets at report_count 1.
